mechanism: Introduces beat-to-beat amplitude alternation in the T-wave to model macroscopic T-wave alternans in severe pathological cases.

name: cardiac_vector_lead_projection
mechanism: Derives multi-lead ECG wave amplitudes by projecting a single 2D cardiac vector's magnitude and angle onto specific lead axes to ensure physiological consistency.
code_snippet: def project_lead(magnitude, angle, lead_angle): return magnitude * np.cos(angle - lead_angle)

name: add_repolarization_lability
mechanism: Introduces stochastic beat-to-beat variation in the QT interval to simulate natural repolarization lability and increase inter-beat diversity.

name: expand_parameter_sampling_ranges
mechanism: Broadens the uniform distribution bounds for physiological parameters, wave morphologies, and noise artifacts to increase inter-sample diversity and restore natural variance.

name: widen_qrs_reduce_r_amplitude
mechanism: Widened the QRS complex components by increasing their standard deviations and reduced the R-wave amplitude to prevent the QRS from dominating the signal energy, thereby restoring the relative prominence of the T-wave.

name: dynamic_t_wave_width_constraint
mechanism: Implements a dynamic scaling constraint on T-wave width parameters to ensure the T-wave fits within the available ST-T window, preventing unrealistic overlap with the QRS complex.
code_snippet: total_width = 2.5 * (sigma_t_left + sigma_t_right) max_width = qt_base - 0.095 if total_width > max_width and max_width > 0: scale = max_width / total_width sigma_t_left *= scale sigma_t_right *= scal

name: constrain_t_wave_axis
mechanism: Clips the T-wave cardiac axis angle to a physiological range to prevent unrealistic T-wave inversions in specific leads.

name: add_respiratory_amplitude_modulation
mechanism: Applies a sinusoidal multiplier driven by the respiratory rate to the amplitudes of all ECG waves to simulate respiratory-induced variations in the cardiac electrical axis and thoracic impedance.
code_snippet: resp_mod = 1.0 + rsa_amp * 1.5 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * resp_rate * beat_t)
